sentence: This project studies how mutant proteins promote leukemogenesis and therapy-resistance by interacting with transcription regulators that remodel chromatin in leukemia-initiating cells.
This project studies how heart tissues differentiate during human development, using a 3D in vitro system, to find DNA sequence elements that drive gene expression.
This project builds instrumental and computational tools to map and measure neuropeptides in tissues using mass spectrometry imaging and ion mobility.
This project builds tools for diffusion MRI that image human brain microstructure at the mesoscopic scale with high image quality.
This project surveys a national sample of peer support specialists to build an index of their work activities and service settings.
This project uses a deep learning model of T cell receptor and antigen interactions to discover therapeutic receptors, find antigens, and develop biomarkers.
This project follows a community cohort to collect symptom screening, respiratory pathogen testing and immunity information, and serves as a data hub for respiratory infections.
This project provides baboons free of adventitious viruses, along with their tissues and expertise, for scientists who study xenotransplantation, vaccines and related dementias.
This project tries to find out which proteins made by astrocytes protect or damage the blood-brain barrier and how they signal through endothelial receptors.
This project improves image-guided radiation therapy of gliomas by using metabolic and structural biomarkers from magnetic resonance spectroscopy imaging to outline tumor boundaries.
This project builds an ultrasound-based device to map and measure periodontal disease in the gingiva.
This project provides a methodology core and a bioinformatics core that support studies of patient cohorts.
This project studies whether cyanotoxins, liver toxins made by cyanobacteria, raise the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, the major form of liver cancer.
This project studies how a chimeric transcription factor suppresses innate immunity in cancer cells by silencing pathways that sense RNA and DNA.
This project runs a core that supports single-cell sequencing and high-dimensional tissue imaging and the analysis of the resulting data.
This project studies how endoplasmic reticulum structure and contact sites with other organelles are regulated in neurons, and how gene mutations disrupt them.
This project builds a resource that gathers information on the genetics, genomics and biology of nematodes, including genes and human disease models.
This project refines an MRI screening protocol to detect aggressive breast cancers early in young women at high risk from inherited risk factors.
This project uses next generation sequencing and a network of clinicians to find genes behind Mendelian conditions whose genes remain unknown.
This project develops an RNA switch that controls when and how much a gene therapy gene is expressed, and tests it in mice.
